key_insight: A physics-informed Fourier-wavelet transformer improves next-step CFD surrogate prediction by combining multiscale spectral encoding with PDE-residual-guided attention and self-supervised pretraining.
engineering_relevance: This could speed up practical fluid simulations while preserving localized wake and interaction structures that matter for design, control, and digital-twin workflows.
method: Hybrid Fourier-wavelet spectral embedding for multiscale flow representation
Physics-biased self-attention driven by PDE residual diagnostics
Self-supervised pretraining with Masked Physics Prediction and Equation Consistency Prediction
evidence_signal: Evaluated on cylinder-wake and fluid-structure-interaction benchmarks, the model achieved the best aggregate performance, including NMSE 0.05875 and PCC 0.97019 on cylinder wake and NMSE 2.70×10^-4 on FSI.
watch_item: Reported gains are benchmark-specific next-step reconstructions, so broader generalization, stability under different meshes/BCs, and training cost should be validated before deployment.
paper_title: A Physics-Informed Fourier-Wavelet Transformer for Multiscale Computational Fluid Dynamics Surrogate Modeling
